page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard2.1 is a virtual machine configuration belonging to the Standard server family. Built upon the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon 8167M processor clocked at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The instance is provisioned with 1 physical core that provides 2 dedicated vCPUs through hyperthreading. It is paired with 15.0 GB of system memory, resulting in an allocation of 7.5 GB of RAM per vCPU.

Hardware accelerators are absent, with the server containing zero GPUs. The configuration does not include bundled local storage, meaning that operational filesystems and persistent storage must be attached via remote block volumes. Network connectivity is supported by 1 complimentary public IPv4 address assigned to the host.

Because the 2 vCPUs use a dedicated allocation rather than a shared or burstable CPU credit model, VM.Standard2.1 delivers consistent processing execution without contention-based throttling. The relatively high memory capacity of 7.5 GB per core presents a cost-efficient profile for setups that are memory-constrained before exhausting CPU capacity, avoiding the need to scale up to higher core tiers merely for memory headroom.

VM.Standard2.1 is suited for workloads that require modest CPU processing coupled with moderate memory requirements. Common operational fits include small relational or in-memory databases, application caching layers, staging environments, lightweight web servers, and background automation tasks.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard2.1 is an entry-level virtual machine instance within the Standard server family, designed for general compute tasks requiring high memory allocation per core. Powered by an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8167M processor operating at 2.0 GHz, the instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with simultaneous multithreading. It includes 15.0 GB of system memory, delivering an elevated ratio of 7.5 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance does not feature integrated local storage or hardware GPU accelerators, necessitating remote block volumes for persistent data needs, while including a single complimentary public IPv4 address. Its configuration presents a cost-effective operational profile for workloads that demand steady processing without CPU bursting. VM.Standard2.1 is well suited for hosting small databases, lightweight web servers, continuous integration workers, caching services, and intermediate memory-bound application tiers.
